transcript: Beau is a new queer musical staged like a band set at a dive bar. Frontman Ace Baker gives us a retelling of his coming of age story through the music that got him through it and a series of flashbacks. It's also about his grandfather Beau who he had thought was deceased, but is still alive and ends up being remarkably influential to Ace's self-actualization. Featuring an ensemble of eight actor-musicians, this show reminded me of Bedlam's Music City and MCC's The Lonely Few in its immersive staging and bar setting. Some songs are stickier than others, but generally the score is quite pleasant and a great vehicle for Matt Rodin’s vocals to soar as Ace. Like a good number of musicals, especially those that are one act and concept-forward, the plot here is a little uneven by having to move so quickly. But, it has a lot of heart, is thematically resonant, and is well-performed. It's worth checking out, and it's always good to support new musicals and support queer art — it's Pride Month, after all. With that another program for my collection.
